title: Big, Little, Happy, Sad
bigQuestion: How do we tell what something is like in Spanish?

story.title: The Elephant and the Mouse
story.kicker: A big elephant and a little mouse find out they can be friends.
paragraphs: In a green park lives an elephant. He is very big. In Spanish we say el elefante grande. That means the big elephant. He is also sad. He has no friends.
Under a rock lives a mouse. She is very little. In Spanish we say la ratona pequeña. That means the little mouse. She is sad too. She is all alone.
One day the mouse sees the elephant. "¡Hola!" she says. The elephant looks down. "¡Hola!" he says. They play all day in the park.
Now the big elephant is feliz. That means happy. The little mouse is feliz too. Big or little, happy or sad, they are good friends now.
story.think: Who is big and who is little in the story? How did they feel at the end?

lessons.title: Grande and Pequeño
lessons.mainIdea: Grande means big. Pequeño means little.
reading: Picture an elephant. It is very big. In Spanish, big is *grande* (big). El elefante grande.
Now picture a mouse. It is very little. Little is *pequeño* (little). El ratón pequeño.
Grande and pequeño are opposites. Opposites mean very different things, like big and little.

words.d: big — el elefante grande, the big elephant
little or small — el ratón pequeño, the little mouse

look.title: Big or Little?
look.text: Look at the playground. There is a big slide and a little ball. There is a big tree and a little bird. The tree is grande. The bird is pequeño.
look.prompt: Name one thing in your room that is grande and one that is pequeño.

check.q: Which word is the opposite of grande?
check.why: Pequeño means little, the opposite of big.
An elephant is very big, so it is grande.

lessons.title: Alto and Bajo
lessons.mainIdea: Alto means tall. Bajo means short.
reading: Picture a giraffe. It is very tall. In Spanish, tall is *alto* (tall). La jirafa is tall.
Now picture a little puppy. It is short. Short is *bajo* (short). Alto and bajo are opposites.
Be careful! Bajo means short, like not tall. It does not mean a short time or a short trip.

words.d: tall — el árbol alto, the tall tree
short (not tall) — el perro bajo, the short dog

look.title: Tall and Short
look.text: Papá stands next to his son Diego. Papá is tall: alto. Diego is short: bajo. Then Diego stands on a chair. "¡Ahora soy alto!" he says. That means "Now I am tall!"
look.prompt: Who in your family is alto? Who is bajo?

check.q: Which word is the opposite of alto?
check.why: Bajo means short, the opposite of tall.

check.q: A very tall tree is el árbol…
check.why: Alto means tall: el árbol alto.

lessons.title: Feliz and Triste
lessons.mainIdea: Feliz means happy. Triste means sad.
reading: Picture a kid at a birthday party. She smiles and laughs. She is *feliz* (happy).
Now picture a kid who lost his ball. He frowns. He is *triste* (sad). Feliz and triste are opposites.
Feliz and triste stay the same for a boy or a girl. El niño feliz. La niña feliz.

words.d: happy — like a smile at a party
sad — like a frown when you lose something

look.title: Faces
look.text: Draw two faces in the air with your finger. The first face has a big smile. It is feliz. The second face has a frown and a tear. It is triste.
look.prompt: Make a feliz face. Now make a triste face. Say each word.

check.q: A kid smiles at a party. The kid is…
check.why: A smiling kid is happy: feliz.

check.q: Which word is the opposite of feliz?
check.why: Triste means sad, the opposite of happy.

lessons.title: The Describing Word Goes After
lessons.mainIdea: In Spanish, the describing word comes after the thing: el perro grande.
reading: In English we say the big dog. Big comes first. In Spanish we say *el perro grande*. Grande comes after!
The thing comes first. Then the describing word. La casa pequeña. El niño feliz. El árbol alto.
English speakers often say el grande perro. That sounds wrong. Say the thing first, then what it is like.

words.d: the big dog — the describing word grande comes after perro

look.title: Thing First
look.text: English: the happy cat. Spanish: el gato feliz. English: the tall tree. Spanish: el árbol alto. English: the sad dog. Spanish: el perro triste. The thing comes first every time.
look.prompt: How do you say the happy dog in Spanish?

check.q: How do you say the big dog?
check.why: In Spanish the describing word goes after the thing: el perro grande.

check.q: What does el gato feliz mean?
check.why: Gato is cat and feliz is happy: the happy cat.

check.q: Which one has the right Spanish order?
check.why: The thing comes first, then the describing word: el árbol alto.

lessons.title: Matching -o and -a
lessons.mainIdea: Describing words ending in -o change to -a to match la words.
reading: Look at a little boy cat. He is el gato *pequeño*. Now look at a little girl cat. She is la gata *pequeña*.
Pequeño ends in o. With la gata it changes to a. The words match. Alto becomes alta. Bajo becomes baja.
Grande, feliz and triste do not end in o. They stay the same. El gato grande. La gata grande.

words.d: little — goes with el words: el gato pequeño
little — goes with la words: la gata pequeña

look.title: Make It Match
look.text: el niño alto, la niña alta. el perro bajo, la casa baja. el gato pequeño, la mesa pequeña. el perro grande, la casa grande. Grande does not change.
look.prompt: How do you say the tall girl? Remember to match the -a.

check.q: How do you say the little house?
check.why: Casa goes with la, so pequeño changes to pequeña, and it goes after: la casa pequeña.
Niña goes with la, so alto changes to alta.

check.q: Which describing word stays the same for el and la?
check.why: Grande does not end in o, so it stays the same: el perro grande, la casa grande.

lessons.title: Many Big Dogs
lessons.mainIdea: When the thing is plural, the describing word gets -s or -es too.
reading: Look at one big dog: el perro grande. Now look at many big dogs: *los perros grandes*. Every word gets an s!
Pequeña becomes pequeñas: las casas pequeñas. Triste becomes tristes: los niños tristes.
Feliz ends in z. Remember the rule? Z changes to c, then add -es. Feliz becomes felices: los gatos felices.

words.d: the big dogs — every word is plural
happy (for many) — feliz changes z to c and adds -es

look.title: Everything Gets an S
look.text: One: el gato pequeño. Many: los gatos pequeños. One: la niña alta. Many: las niñas altas. One: el niño feliz. Many: los niños felices. Count the s sounds!
look.prompt: Say the plural of la casa grande.

check.q: What is the plural of el perro grande?
check.why: Every word becomes plural: los perros grandes.

check.q: What is the plural of feliz?
check.why: Z changes to c, then add -es: felices.

check.q: Which one means the little houses?
check.why: Casas goes with las and -a, and everything is plural: las casas pequeñas.

review.q: How do you say the sad dog?
review.why: The describing word goes after the thing: el perro triste.
Gata goes with la, so pequeño becomes pequeña.

review.q: In the story, how is the elephant at the end?
review.why: At the end the elephant has a friend, so he is feliz, happy.

review.q: What is the opposite of alto?
review.why: Alto means tall and bajo means short.

review.q: What is the plural of el niño feliz?
review.why: Everything is plural, and feliz changes z to c before -es: los niños felices.
